findings.title: Web actuator endpoints ship with show-values: always, letting any authenticated ROLE_USER read the JWT signing secret and admin password; the stolen HMAC secret allows offline pinpointJwt forgery and ROLE_ADMIN escalation on /api/admin/**
findings.preconditions: Stock deployment with the documented basic-login mode enabled (pinpoint.modules.web.login=basicLogin, the vendor-recommended authentication mode). Attacker holds any valid low-privilege ROLE_USER account. The actuator management server is reachable to the attacker (management.server.port=8443, bound by default in the shipped web-starter configuration; no role rule restricts /monitor). No administrator misconfiguration is required: management.endpoint.env/configprops show-values: always and the missing /monitor-specific authorization rule are shipped defaults in web-starter/src/main/resources/application.yml.
findings.positiveControl: Authenticated ROLE_USER GET http://<web>:8443/monitor/env returned HTTP 200 with 34,728 bytes of Spring Environment properties including the configured values web.security.auth.jwt.secretkey, web.security.auth.user, web.security.auth.admin and admin.password verbatim (dummy values planted for the test were all found byte-for-byte). Using the read secret, an HS256 pinpointJwt with userId=<admin-username> and userRole=[ROLE_ADMIN] was forged offline; with that cookie GET /api/admin/agentIdMap returned HTTP 200 whereas the same request with a real ROLE_USER cookie returned HTTP 403 and with no cookie returned HTTP 302.
findings.negativeControl: Anonymous GET /monitor/env on 8443 returned HTTP 302 redirect to /login (the basic-login filter chain covers the management server). A request carrying a garbage pinpointJwt cookie to the same URL also returned 302. The privilege-escalation step was differential: forged-admin cookie 200 vs real-ROLE_USER-cookie 403 vs no-cookie 302 on the identical /api/admin request.
findings.observedImpact: Full privilege escalation from ROLE_USER to ROLE_ADMIN on the web application: the forged token grants /api/admin/** (destructive admin operations such as application/agent data deletion), and the same env output discloses admin.password used by the second admin gate. The JWT secret also allows minting tokens for any username for the 12-hour token lifetime (logout only deletes the cookie; there is no server-side revocation).
findings.notDemonstrated: Not demonstrated: destructive /api/admin write operations were not executed (the escalation proof uses one read-only authenticated route whose authorization outcome differs by cookie state: 302/403/500); impact on deployments where basic login is disabled (app is then anonymous by a separate documented design) was not tested; exploitation was performed only against the local Docker lab; no released-version sweep. A transient 302-flap of the lab under sibling-container load is documented in evidence/f1-flap-note.txt.

findings.title: Shipped server.error configuration (include-exception/message/binding-errors/stacktrace: always) plus an in-repo @ControllerAdvice disclose full internal stack traces and request parameters to unauthenticated callers via the permitAll /api-public/error path
findings.preconditions: Stock deployment; the error-disclosure settings and the /api-public permitAll error path are shipped defaults in web-starter/src/main/resources/application.yml and web/src/main/resources/problem/. Attacker needs only network reachability to the web port; no account is required.
findings.positiveControl: Anonymous GET /api-public/error on the stock web container returned HTTP 200 with an RFC 7807 body whose trace property contained a full ~60-frame Java stack trace (internal package names, Spring Security filter chain classes, Tomcat internals), and whose properties echoed the request method, parameters and the container hostname.
findings.negativeControl: The same request was confirmed to hit the public path without authentication by design (permitAll rule for /api-public/** in basic-login/src/main/java/.../PinpointBasicLoginConfig.java). Negative control for the disclosure knob itself is source-level: setting include-stacktrace to never removes the trace property (Spring Boot ErrorAttributes behavior); this knob-off state was not separately run in the lab and is recorded under Not demonstrated.
findings.observedImpact: Unauthenticated disclosure of internal class names, library versions, filter-chain structure, absolute framework internals and request-echoed parameters. Useful for reconnaissance in chained attacks; no direct confidentiality breach of business data was observed.
findings.notDemonstrated: Not demonstrated: the knob-off negative control was not executed in the lab; no business-data leakage via this path was shown; stack traces from exception-carrying endpoints (e.g. storage failures) were not triggered because HBase was unavailable in the lab, so only the framework-level 404 handler output was captured.
